newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon t-bill auction raises 284.5 bln pounds.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon t-bill auction raises 284.5 bln pounds.

text.p: Lebanon's weekly treasury bill issue of July 10 raised 284.5 billion Lebanese pounds, according to finance ministry results issued on Monday.
The previous issue raised 266.4 billion pounds.
The issue posted a nominal surplus of subscription against maturity of 62.74 billion pounds. It raised the following amounts (in billion of pounds, previous week in brackets):

The central bank said seven percent of all competitive bids -- those made by Lebanese institutions -- were accepted up to the discount rate and yield for three-month bills, 17 percent for six-month bills, and 50 percent for one-year bills.
The bank restricted the acceptance of all competitive bids for the two-year bills approving only 70 percent.

It also restricted the acceptance of non-competitive bids -- those made by private individuals and foreign investors -- for the shorter-term bills, approving seven percent up to the discount rate and yield for three-month bills and 17 percent for six-month bills.
All non-competitive bids were approved for longer-term bills.
The Lebanese pound closed at 1,538.75 to the U.S. dollar on Monday from 1,539.25 a week earlier and 1,569 a year ago.
